newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil gains on futures, diesel shows strength.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil gains on futures, diesel shows strength.

text.p: NWE gas oil rose on Friday, bolstered by stronger futures and significantly firmer diesel premiums.
May IPE gas oil was $1.50 a tonne stronger at $166.25 at 1200 GMT, playing catch-up to Brent's late gains on Thursday.
Traders said diesel premiums have strengthened by $1-2 a tonne with a bid of May IPE +$13.50 cif NWE heard.
"Yesterday's offer of May IPE +$14 has disappeared and I think $14 may get done today," said one trader.
Barge premiums were a touch stronger with 2,000 tonnes sold at May IPE +$10.50 fob Rotterdam.
Diesel's strength was attributed to tight supply and the expectation that supplies will not improve in the near term.
Heating oil barges were very quiet, with low Rhine water levels keeping German buyers sidelined. Traders said it was not surprising Friday was slower after a fairly eventful week.
Barges were pegged steady at around May IPE +50 cents fob ARA for refinery material and flat for storage.
